title: scim-optimistic-ack-and-manual-remediation-ui-for-failed-deprovisions
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: When SCIM deprovisioning calls to downstream identity providers or directory connectors intermittently fail, the system currently either retries automatically (risking duplicate operations) or marks the work item as 'failed' with insufficient operator context. This ticket implements an optimistic-acknowledgment flow to avoid blocking user-visible progress while surfacing a deterministic remediation path for operators via a manual remediation UI and enriched audit trails.
background: We continue to see incidents where deprovision requests (user/group delete or remove) time out or partially succeed across heterogeneous identity providers. Existing playbooks rely on ad-hoc reconciliation jobs and log searches. This causes delayed access removal for high-risk accounts and noisy on-call paging. Previous tickets addressed backoff/retry strategies, but we lack an operator-forward recovery surface and a safe optimistic ACK that prevents double-deletes while preserving traceability.
goals: 1) Add an optimistic acknowledgment semantics for SCIM write operations so API callers see timely success when the operation is durable at our ingestion layer. 2) Surface failed downstream operations in a dedicated operator UI with clear remediation actions (retry, mark-resolved, rollback-reconcile). 3) Attach structured audit events and an immutable shadow log per provisioning operation to improve post-mortem and compliance reports.
acceptance_criteria: API: SCIM write path returns 202+optimistic-ack when request persisted to durable queue; response contains operation_id and remediation handle
Operator UI: List view with filters (status, tenant, action-type, age) and actions: retry, escalate, mark-resolved; actions create new audit events
Idempotency: Retried operations are deduplicated by operation_id and skeleton idempotency checks documented
Audit: Every optimistic-ack and every downstream failure produces structured audit records in audit-logs storage with correlation keys for tenant/operation/request-id
SLOs: Successful optimistic-ack latency under 150ms; background delivery retry/backoff respects tenant rate limits
Security: UI actions require RBAC v2 Admin role; all actions logged for compliance
E2E tests: Simulated downstream failure scenarios in CI with operator action workflows validated
design_notes: We will implement an 'ingestion durable queue' (existing Kafka topic + per-tenant partitioning) where the SCIM API writes canonical operations. The optimistic ACK will be returned after the write is durably acknowledged. Downstream workers will be responsible for delivery with enhanced visibility. The operator UI will re-use the console's rollout framework and add a remediation panel that references the shadow logs. Avoid exposing raw provider errors to the UI; instead map to normalized failure codes and remediation suggestions.
technical_approach: API change: SCIM POST/PUT/DELETE returns 202 with {operation_id, status: 'pending'}. Add header X-Redwood-Operation-Id for cross-service tracing.
Durability: Persist canonical operation to existing provision-ops Kafka topic with replication=3; ensure consumer offsets are committed after downstream ack.

Delivery worker: Enhance scim-delivery service to record per-attempt metadata (attempt_ts, provider_response_code, provider_error_snippet) into shadow-log table in Postgres; implement exponential backoff with tenant-aware rate cap
Idempotency: Include operation_id + scim_resource_version; workers must perform provider-safe conditional deletes (Etag/If-Match) when supported
Operator UI: New 'Remediation' tab in Console -> Security -> SCIM with a paginated list and detail flyout. Integrate A/B testing for layout before GA
Audit: Write structured audit events to audit-logs pipeline (Cloud Storage + BigQuery) with schema: operation_id, tenant, actor, original_request, optimistic_ack_ts, final_status
RBAC: Gate UI buttons via RBAC v2 policy 'scim:operator:remediate' and validate via token introspection
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable optimistic-ack only for internal admin tenants and 5 pilot customers; monitor drop in API latency and number of failed downstream deliveries
Phase 2 (limited): Open to all self-serve tenants but UI actions disabled; metrics collection and alerting live
Phase 3 (GA): Operator UI enabled for RBAC v2 admins; promote to release auth-2026.03
Rollback: The API maintains backwards-compatible behaviour behind a feature flag; disable optimistic-ack to fall back to synchronous delivery if needed
test_plan: Unit tests for operation persistence and operation_id generation
Integration test: simulate provider 503/timeout and assert optimistic-ack and shadow-log entries
Load test: ensure optimistic-ack scale under 2000 ops/s for dedicated tenants
Security test: RBAC enforcement tests and audit-event tamper checks
Manual QA: Operator flows (retry, mark-resolved) with mock downstream connectors
open_questions: Q1: Should optimistic-ack be the default for all write types (create/update/delete) or only for deletes/deprovisions?
Q2: What retention window for shadow-log rows is required for compliance (90 days vs 1 year)?
Q3: How do we display partial successes for group membership changes (some providers may accept a subset)?
Q4: Are there provider-specific idempotency guarantees we should encode in connector adapters?
